selection_policy.reason: Start with a washer because repeated useful cycles, energy/water use, wear items, and repair tasks can be measured without opening a sealed refrigerant circuit; mains, water, heat, weight, and rotating hazards still require qualified design review and controlled testing.

common_architecture_hypotheses.proposal: Expose reversible service access to high-incidence maintenance and repair parts, with stable part/revision identifiers, manuals, task scripts, and post-repair tests.
common_architecture_hypotheses.success_condition: Matched-control studies show lower total restoration time/cost or waste after accounting for the added panels, fasteners, interfaces, inventory and failure modes.
failure_modes: access panels weaken structure or leak barrier
extra connectors/seals add new faults
module replacement wastes larger assemblies than necessary

common_architecture_hypotheses.proposal: Separate user maintenance, wet-system work, mains/high-current work, heavy/rotating mechanisms, hot/pressurized systems, and refrigerant circuits into clearly documented service boundaries.
common_architecture_hypotheses.success_condition: Task trials and qualified hazard review confirm that each task has an explicit isolation procedure, permitted role, stop condition, and post-service verification.
failure_modes: easy access is misinterpreted as DIY authorization
isolation or stored energy is missed
service boundaries hide critical inspection points

common_architecture_hypotheses.proposal: Evaluate component replacement, repairable subassembly, and whole-module replacement against repair time, service cost, waste, stock, service life and interface overhead.
common_architecture_hypotheses.success_condition: Chosen boundary lowers robust life-cycle cost or improves restoration while maintaining function, reliability and safety.
failure_modes: oversized module replacement wastes parts
small-part repair requires costly diagnosis/labour
special module inventory delays restoration

common_architecture_hypotheses.proposal: Expose offline fault isolation, safe measurement points, sensor freshness/units, diagnostic limits and evidence receipts without cloud or vendor account dependency.
common_architecture_hypotheses.success_condition: Technicians and permitted users can distinguish command, observation, hypothesis and verified function; missing/conflicting evidence triggers abstention.
failure_modes: measurement points expose hazardous energy
sensor faults masquerade as product faults
diagnostic UI implies a safety verdict or overstates certainty

common_architecture_hypotheses.proposal: Define interfaces and substitute part qualification by exact host revision, electrical/fluid/mechanical/thermal ratings, installation instructions and post-installation test.
common_architecture_hypotheses.success_condition: Approved alternate supply can be installed and validated without relying on guessed pinouts, nominal dimensions or family branding.
failure_modes: interface standard overgeneralizes compatibility
alternate part affects EMC, thermal, leakage, vibration or safety performance
obsolete part has no traceable approved substitute

common_architecture_hypotheses.proposal: Evaluate energy, water and consumables per unit of successfully delivered function under a declared and repeatable workload.
common_architecture_hypotheses.success_condition: Resource improvements hold while functional performance remains inside preregistered non-inferiority margins and no critical failure metric regresses.
failure_modes: efficiency claim hides lower cleaning/heating/cooling performance
one test cycle is not representative of lifetime use
instrument uncertainty masks or reverses claimed gain

freeze_before_test: exact make/model/revision and condition of each control and candidate unit
workload, ambient and installation conditions, cycle/draw profiles, inclusion/exclusion and stopping rules
instrument identity, calibration status, uncertainty, placement and raw-data format
repair task scripts, permitted role, tools, isolation steps and post-repair verification
cost model, location, price date, utility tariff, service labour, part/shipping cost and downtime horizon
analysis plan, missing-data treatment, per-fault reporting, confidence intervals and non-inferiority margin
metrics: functional output and critical outcome integrity
energy, water, consumables and standby/losses under matched useful output
median and P90 total restore time, including diagnosis, travel, part delay, rework and verification
repair success, failed attempts, residual defects and recurrence at a defined follow-up horizon
parts/labour/shipping cost, waste, repair-unit size and discarded mass
user-maintenance task success within explicitly permitted task boundary
sourcing: stock status, number of viable suppliers, price date, delivery time and qualified substitutes
safety and conformity evidence reported as separate gates, never averaged into a composite performance score

proposed_targets.target: At least 25% lower median and P90 total restore time on a preregistered common-fault set versus frozen retail controls.
proposed_targets.guardrail: No increase in critical safety failures, repeat faults or functional-output regression.

proposed_targets.target: At least 90% successful completion of approved normal-user maintenance tasks in a representative usability test.
proposed_targets.guardrail: Exclude mains internals, sealed refrigerant, pressure systems and any task not approved for user service.

proposed_targets.target: At least 90% first-visit repair success on the scoped qualified-service task set.
proposed_targets.guardrail: Report by fault class and include failed attempts, uncertain diagnosis and repeat service.

proposed_targets.target: Demonstrate lower expected cost of delivered function after module, interface, inventory, service, energy/water and downtime costs.
proposed_targets.guardrail: Show sensitivity intervals; no superiority claim if plausible assumptions reverse the conclusion.

proposed_targets.target: Explore a 5–10% resource-use improvement at matched useful output as a hypothesis.
proposed_targets.guardrail: Function and safety non-inferiority margins must be preregistered; energy/water use alone cannot hide poorer output.

proposed_targets.target: Design for a 10-year parts-support commitment for the chosen open reference design.
proposed_targets.guardrail: This is a design goal, not a statement that the same legal duty applies in every market or appliance category.

proposed_targets.target: Zero unsafe next-test/repair recommendations in the finite adversarial contract suite.
proposed_targets.guardrail: Critical faults are separate hard gates with conservative abstention/referral; no average may hide a miss.

proposed_targets.target: Replicate key functional/serviceability results on at least three candidate units and with at least one independent test team for stronger claims.
proposed_targets.guardrail: Three units are only a pilot floor; expand sample size based on observed variance and the claim being made.

no_claims: Do not claim a 10-year physical lifetime from a short accelerated test without validating the failure mechanism.
Do not treat simulation, a signed record, a planned part or a completed work order as physical proof of function restoration or safety.
Do not call an appliance DIY-repairable merely because parts are removable; task, hazard, tools, role and post-test requirements must be specified.

families.name: Front-load washing machine / washer-dryer
families.why: Recommended first large-appliance engineering target: repeated measurable cycles, consequential repair failures, clearly identifiable wear/service components and no sealed refrigerant circuit in a plain washer.
architecture_hypotheses: Compare conventional machine with improved documentation against a front/side service spine for pump, valve, heater, door lock, sensors, controller and drive.
Compare a bolted/serviceable tub with separate bearing/seal replacement against a welded tub requiring larger assembly replacement; evaluate leak integrity, vibration, cost, waste and service time.
Compare belt/direct-drive options at matched cleaning, rinse, spin, noise, energy and service outcomes; do not assume either is universally better.
Evaluate whether optional external hot-water input is useful only for declared installations and verified energy, temperature-control, backflow and scald-safety constraints.
user_maintenance_tasks: clean drain/coin filter using documented isolation and water-capture steps
clean detergent dispenser and accessible door seal
inspect external inlet/drain hoses for visible damage or leakage
run documented non-invasive user diagnostics
qualified_service_tasks: mains/heater/controller/drive repair and electrical protective checks
drum/tub/suspension/bearing repair and heavy assembly handling
powered spin, imbalance and leakage verification after repair
pressure/temperature-related internal service
function_metrics: cleaning and rinsing quality per declared laundry load
litres per successfully cleaned kg and kWh per load
spin-drying outcome and cycle duration
leakage, vibration and noise
task time, first-visit repair and recurrence
bearing/tub replacement cost and material discarded
hazards: mains electricity combined with water and heating elements
heavy rotating drum, imbalance, pinch/crush and tip hazards

families.name: Household dishwasher
families.why: A strong second target because it combines measurable cleaning, drying, energy and water outcomes with replaceable wet-system parts and meaningful service downtime.
architecture_hypotheses: Compare front-access filter/sump and replaceable circulation/drain pumps with whole-sump cartridge replacement; count interface and waste costs.
Provide service access to spray arms, door seals, valves, sensors, heater and controller without destructive panel removal.
Include a defined leak-capture/detection path and a reproducible post-repair leak and cleaning verification protocol.
user_maintenance_tasks: clean filter and removable spray arms
maintain salt/rinse aid where present per manual
clean accessible door seal and check external hoses
use documented non-invasive fault indicators
qualified_service_tasks: internal pump/valve/heater/harness repair
mains/wet-area electrical isolation and checks
leak tray diagnosis and post-repair leak/cleaning tests
function_metrics: correctly cleaned place settings per kWh and litre
drying outcome and eco-programme duration
leak detection and post-repair leak integrity
repair task time, parts price, restoration cost and recurrence
hazards: leak/flood damage and hot wash water

families.name: Refrigerator / freezer
families.why: High lifetime electricity and food-preservation consequences make repairability valuable, but the sealed refrigerant system and temperature-safety outcomes require a distinct qualified-service track.
architecture_hypotheses: Design independently replaceable gasket, hinge, fan, drain, defrost element, sensor, light and electronic control/inverter modules.
Provide safe access for airflow-path and condenser maintenance without exposing live parts.
Compare component-level electronic repair against a replaceable control module including diagnostic quality, cost, electronic waste and downtime.
Explore any sealed-circuit module replacement only after qualified refrigerant, leakage, thermal, transport, reliability and lifecycle review; do not assume quick couplers or DIY refrigerant service.
user_maintenance_tasks: inspect and clean/replace door gasket per manual
clean specified external airflow/condenser area while isolated
clean approved defrost drain and removable interior components
monitor displayed temperature and documented user alerts
qualified_service_tasks: sealed refrigerant circuit, compressor or refrigerant charging/recovery work
mains/inverter/capacitor and protective electrical checks
temperature-control, defrost and post-repair pull-down/recovery verification
function_metrics: annualized kWh per usable litre under declared use/ambient profile
temperature stability, door-open recovery and compartment-safe range
gasket replacement time, defrost/drain reliability and noise
repair cost, food-outage/spoilage risk, parts lead time and recurrence
hazards: refrigerant identity, pressure and potentially flammable refrigerants depending on design

families.name: Heat-pump tumble dryer
families.why: Heat recovery can improve running economics, while airflow/lint/condensate access and repair-unit size materially affect maintenance and service costs.
architecture_hypotheses: Make lint filters, airflow cleaning points, condensate system, drum drive, blower, door seal, sensors and controller separately serviceable where a trade study supports it.
Compare replaceable sealed heat-pump assembly versus qualified component repair; include refrigerant service cost, parts availability, leak checks and waste.
Design maintenance paths so cleaning does not require destructive opening or casual access to high-temperature and mains components.
user_maintenance_tasks: clean user lint filter and accessible secondary filter
empty/clean condensate container and approved drain path
clean door seal and run approved user diagnostic
qualified_service_tasks: mains/heater/thermal interlock and internal blower repair
sealed heat-pump/refrigerant circuit service
post-repair airflow, moisture-removal and thermal-protection verification
function_metrics: kWh per kg water removed at fixed endpoint
residual moisture, cycle time and condensation performance
airflow restriction/overheating protection checks
filter task success/time, repair cost and recurrence

families.name: Heat-pump water heater
families.why: Potential for meaningful water-heating energy savings and high downtime consequences, but combines a water tank, hot water, pressure-relief, corrosion and refrigerant-service constraints.
architecture_hypotheses: Compare integrated system against a factory-sealed heat-pump top module with a separate tank; evaluate service time alongside standby loss, seal count, material, cost and compatibility.
Make fan/air filter, condensate, sensors and controls serviceable without opening refrigerant circuit.
Provide traceable access and instructions for manufacturer-specified tank maintenance, anode and replaceable components.
user_maintenance_tasks: clean only manufacturer-approved air filter and condensate path
record leaks, displayed status and water-temperature symptoms
perform user-level inspection without opening pressure boundaries
qualified_service_tasks: mains, element, thermostat and control work
water-side plumbing, tank drain, pressure relief and hot-water service
sealed refrigerant circuit and heat-pump commissioning
verified recovery, temperature and leakage checks
function_metrics: delivered hot-water heat per kWh under declared draw/ambient profile
COP/recovery rate, first-hour delivery, standby loss and temperature stability
maintenance time, corrosion/scale findings, leakage and restoration cost
hazards: scalding hot water, stored pressure and pressure-relief hazards

families.name: Residential air-source heat-pump HVAC
families.why: Large energy and comfort impact, but commissioning, building envelope/load, climate, high voltage and refrigerant handling make attribution and validation much harder than the first appliance pilot.
architecture_hypotheses: Separate traceable service assemblies for filters/indoor blower, outdoor fan, sensors, controls/inverter and condensate system where the interfaces and failure data justify it.
Give qualified technicians a clean diagnostic/commissioning workflow and published compatible-part requirements; never make refrigerant quick connection a DIY assumption.
Compare service-board/module replacement with qualified board-level repair and whole-unit replacement under matched climate/load/installation conditions.
user_maintenance_tasks: clean/replace permitted filters
keep approved airflow clearances and clean user-accessible surfaces
observe and record alarms, noise and comfort symptoms
qualified_service_tasks: mains/high-voltage/inverter and capacitor service
refrigerant leak, recovery, charging, brazing or sealed circuit work
outdoor unit lifting and electrical installation/commissioning
post-service capacity, leak and protection verification
function_metrics: seasonal heating/cooling electricity at matched delivered capacity
capacity and comfort stability across declared ambient range
defrost, noise, condensate/leak and refrigerant-service outcomes
diagnostic/service duration, travel, parts delay and recurrence
hazards: pressurized refrigerant and possible flammability depending on refrigerant
working at height, lifting, outdoor exposure and installation-specific hazards

washer_architecture_variants.hypothesis: A matched retail washer establishes function, service, energy and cost baselines without assuming the proposed design is better.
required_measurements: cleaning and rinsing outcome under a fixed soil/load profile
water use, energy use, cycle duration and spin-drying outcome
access/disassembly/service task time and tools
parts price, delivery, labour, rework and restoration time
leakage, vibration/noise and defined post-repair verification
failure_modes: control set is not comparable in capacity, age, market or load profile
published label values are mistaken for measurements under our benchmark protocol
control service history is missing or selection is biased toward easy-to-repair models

washer_architecture_variants.hypothesis: Reversible access panels, labelled interfaces and a well-designed service manual may reduce repair effort without changing the core wet tub or drive architecture.
required_measurements: panel opening and reassembly time
common-task service time and damaged-fastener rate
harness damage, strain relief and leakage after reassembly
functional test parity and post-repair recurrence
added part count, BOM cost, vibration/noise and material burden
failure_modes: access panels reduce structural stiffness or sealing
additional fasteners or harness routing add new failure modes
documentation improves steps but does not improve diagnosis or total restoration time

washer_architecture_variants.hypothesis: A dedicated service path to the pump/filter, inlet valve, dispenser, door lock, heater/sensor harness, controller and drive may improve fault isolation and replacement time if interfaces do not add excessive cost or failure points.
required_measurements: access and replacement time by module
connector/seal failure and misconnection rate during test assembly
post-repair leak, protective electrical and functional verification
module price/inventory, parts wait and discarded mass per repair
total restore-time median/P90 and recurrence by fault class
failure_modes: a replaceable module contains expensive components that were not faulty
connectors, seals or rigid interfaces become frequent new failure points
diagnostic boundaries do not align with actual fault-localization evidence

washer_architecture_variants.hypothesis: A bolted outer tub and separately serviceable bearing/seal assembly may reduce replacement cost and waste, but only if sealing, vibration, fatigue, assembly precision and recurrence remain acceptable.
required_measurements: bearing/seal replacement time and required tools
static leak and repeat-cycle seal integrity
loaded spin vibration, noise, imbalance and temperature
replacement-part cost and mass discarded
repeat-failure rate and sensitivity to assembly tolerance
failure_modes: serviceable joint leaks or loosens under thermal/mechanical cycling
bearing replacement precision demands costly fixtures or expert labour
lower initial material waste is offset by lower joint reliability or higher assembly cost

washer_architecture_variants.hypothesis: Belt and direct-drive options must be compared at matched cleaning, rinsing, spin, noise, resource and repair outcomes before a topology is selected.
compare_against: at least one accessible candidate architecture
required_measurements: energy and cycle performance under matched loads
speed control, vibration, acoustic noise and imbalance response
drive/belt/coupling repair time and parts availability
controller/inverter cost, failure modes and electronic waste
post-repair loaded-spin verification and recurrence
failure_modes: topology comparison is confounded by motor sizing, control firmware or drum design
the apparently simpler drive transfers cost into the controller or specialized service
the test rewards peak efficiency while degrading spin quality, noise or reliability
